review_candidates.description: About Enline Enline is a fast-growing deeptech company that builds sensorless digital twins for power grids and renewable energy assets. Our platform helps transmission and distribution operators, as well as wind and solar plant owners, increase output, reduce losses, and improve grid reliability—with zero new hardware. Our solutions combine power systems engineering, AI, and high-performance simulations to deliver actionable recommendations for asset control and optimization. We’re helping grid operators and renewable producers worldwide meet the challenges of a clean energy future, and we’re looking for talented people to join us. About The Role We are hiring Software Engineers (mid and senior) who have built or integrated real grid software: SCADA, Advanced Distribution Management Systems (ADMS) or Distributed Energy Resource Management Systems (DERMS). You will design, build, integrate and run software that connects to field devices, control-centre systems and grid-edge assets. Some of it runs in real time where reliability and security cannot be compromised. You will also use AI-assisted development tools every day, and you will be responsible for checking that what they produce is correct and safe. We want engineers who move faster with these tools without lowering the bar for code quality in a critical-infrastructure setting. Requirements: Key Responsibilities Design, develop and maintain software components for SCADA, ADMS, DMS/OMS/EMS and DERMS platforms, including real-time data acquisition, telemetry processing, control and dispatch logic. Build and maintain integrations with field devices and control systems over industrial and utility protocols such as DNP3, IEC 60870-5-104, IEC 61850 (MMS, GOOSE) and Modbus. Integrate grid-edge and DER systems (solar PV, battery storage, EV charging, flexible loads) using standards such as IEEE 2030.5, OpenADR, IEEE 1547 and SunSpec/Modbus, as well as vendor and aggregator APIs. Model and exchange network data with the Common Information Model (CIM, IEC 61968 / IEC 61970), including network-model import, versioning and integration with GIS, OMS and asset systems. Build reliable, low-latency services for real-time and near-real-time workloads (event processing, state estimation inputs, alarming, historians, time-series data). Apply secure-by-design practices for operational technology (OT) environments, following utility cybersecurity requirements such as NERC CIP, IEC 62351, IEC 62443 and the EU NIS2 directive where they apply. Write automated tests: unit, integration, protocol simulation, hardware/software-in-the-loop where needed, and regression tests for control logic. Use AI-assisted development tools daily to speed up design, coding, testing, refactoring and documentation, and review, test and validate every AI-generated change before it is merged. Take part in code reviews, architecture discussions, on-call/incident response for production systems (per team rotation) and post-incident reviews. Work with power-systems engineers, control-room operators, product managers and utility customers to turn operational needs into working software. Senior level, additionally: lead the technical design of major components, set engineering standards (including team practices for the safe use of AI tools), mentor other engineers and represent engineering in customer and partner technical discussions. Basic Qualifications Grid software experience (required): Hands-on experience building or integrating grid software, such as SCADA, ADMS, and/or DERMS (or closely related OMS, DMS, EMS or microgrid-controller platforms), in a commercial, utility or production setting. Experience level: Mid-level: about 3+ years of professional software engineering, including at least 1–2 years on grid / utility / energy systems. Senior: about 6+ years of professional software engineering, including at least 3 years on grid / utility / energy systems, with evidence of technical leadership. Strong skills in at least one production language commonly used in this field, e.g. C++, Python, Go or Rust. Working knowledge of at least one utility/industrial communication protocol: DNP3, IEC 60870-5-104, IEC 61850 or Modbus. Understanding of real-time or near-real-time system design: concurrency, latency, fault tolerance, high availability and redundancy. Experience with relational and/or time-series databases and with messaging/event-streaming (e.g. Kafka, MQTT, AMQP). Good engineering habits: version control (Git), automated testing, CI/CD and code review. Awareness of security in critical infrastructure / OT environments. Professional working proficiency in English (written and spoken), Portuguese is good to have. AI Proficiency Requirement (required) This is a firm requirement for all levels. Candidates must show: Daily, hands-on use of AI-assisted development tools such as Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Claude Code or similar, as a normal part of their workflow (writing code, tests, refactoring, debugging, documentation or exploring an unfamiliar codebase). The ability to critically review and validate AI-generated code. This includes spotting incorrect logic, invented ("hallucinated") APIs or protocol details, security weaknesses, performance problems and missing edge cases, and backing changes up with tests before they reach production. Good judgement about when not to rely on AI output, especially for safety-critical control logic, protocol implementations, security-sensitive code and anything that could affect grid operations Responsible use: following company policies on code confidentiality, customer data and approved tools, and never pasting sensitive operational data or credentials into unapproved tools. During the interview process we will ask you to walk us through how you use these tools and to review a piece of AI-generated code. Preferred Qualifications Experience with grid platforms (for example from GE Vernova, Siemens, Schneider Electric, Hitachi Energy, Oracle Utilities, AspenTech/OSI, Survalent, Efacec or similar) or with DERMS / virtual power plant (VPP) platforms. Knowledge of power-systems concepts: load flow / power flow, state estimation, fault location, isolation and service restoration (FLISR), Volt/VAR optimisation (VVO), hosting capacity and switching/outage management. Experience with CIM (IEC 61968 / 61970) network models and CGMES, and integration with GIS (e.g. Esri ArcGIS, Smallworld) and asset management systems. Experience with IEEE 2030.5, OpenADR 2.0 / 3.0, IEEE 1547, OCPP (EV charging) or flexibility-market integrations. Hands-on experience meeting NERC CIP, IEC 62351, IEC 62443 or NIS2 requirements in delivered systems. Cloud and platform experience (AWS, Azure or GCP; Kubernetes; infrastructure as code) and hybrid on-premises/cloud deployments common in utilities. Experience with historians and time-series platforms (e.g. AVEVA PI, InfluxDB, TimescaleDB). Experience building internal AI tooling, agent workflows or evaluation and guardrails for AI-assisted development in a regulated environment. Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Electrical/Power Engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Portuguese, Spanish or other European languages are a plus, but not required.
